chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'When is the sacrifice made?' He said, 'When the Imam departs.' I said, 'And if I am in a land where there is no Imam, and I lead them in congregation prayer,' he said, 'When the sun has reached its zenith.' And he said, 'There is no harm in you praying alone, and there is no prayer except with an Imam.'
ai.seo_question: When should the Eid sacrifice be performed if there is no Imam present?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal sequence of the Eid sacrifice, distinguishing between the presence of a designated Imam and local congregational leadership. It establishes that the sacrifice is valid only after the sun has passed its zenith (istiqlal), ensuring the prayer is fully concluded, while simultaneously affirming the necessity of an Imam for valid congregational prayer, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence.
